exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Greatest Common Divisor of Two Three-Digit Numbers

question.text: Find the greatest common divisor of $506$ and $207.$
question.explanation:
We use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows:

\begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 506 & = & 207(2) & + & 92 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 207 & = & 92(2) & + & {\color{red}23} \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 92 & = &23(4) & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*}

The last positive remainder is ${\color{red}23}.$ Therefore, we conclude that the greatest common divisor of $506$ and $207$ is $23.$ Symbolically, we write

\[ \textrm{gcd}(506,207) = 23. \]

exampleAnswers.title: Determining Whether Two Integers are Coprime

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\textrm{gcd}(888, 205) = 7$
  2. $\textrm{gcd}(888, 205) = 1$
  3. $888$ and $205$ are coprime
question.explanation:
Recall that two integers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is $1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false, while statement II is true. Indeed, let's use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows: \begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 888 & = & 205\cdot 4 & + & 68 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 205& = & 68 \cdot 3 & + & {\color{blue}1} \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 68 & = &1 \cdot 68 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*} The last positive remainder is ${\color{blue}1}.$ So, the greatest common divisor of $888$ and $205$ is $1\mathbin{:}$ \[ \textrm{gcd}(888, 205) = 1. \]

  • Statement III is true. Since $\textrm{gcd}(888, 205) = 1,$ the numbers are coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

example.title: Determining Whether Two Integers are Coprime

question.text:
Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\textrm{gcd}(321, 213) = 3$
  2. $\textrm{gcd}(321, 213) = 1$
  3. $321$ and $213$ are coprime
question.explanation:
Recall that two integers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is $1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true, while statement II is false. Indeed, let's use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows: \begin{align*} \begin{matrix} 321 & = & 213 \cdot 1 & + & 108 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 213 & = & 108 \cdot 1 & + & 105 \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 108 & = &105 \cdot 1 & + & {\color{blue}3} \\ & \swarrow & & \swarrow & \\ 105 & = &3 \cdot 35 & + & 0 \\ \end{matrix} \end{align*} The last positive remainder is ${\color{blue}3}.$ So, the greatest common divisor of $321$ and $213$ is $3\mathbin{:}$ \[ \textrm{gcd}(321, 213) = 3. \]

  • Statement III is false. Since $\textrm{gcd}(321, 213) > 1,$ the numbers are not coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

  • Statement III is true. Since $\textrm{gcd}(243, 167) = 1,$ the numbers are coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
